pathway.title: Builders FirstSource, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Reported leverage has risen sharply. Debt principal at September 30, 2026 was USD 4,658.904 million against USD 4,485.046 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of USD 173.858 million driven by USD 197.0 million of revolver borrowing, while twelve-month reported EBITDA was USD 904.402 million against USD 1,377.708 million in FY2025. The debt is mostly fixed-rate senior unsecured notes with no scheduled principal payment before 2030, so leverage moves with earnings: total debt to EBITDA is 5.15x versus 3.26x and net debt to EBITDA 5.09x versus 3.12x (Documentary Fact, CP-1 leverage chart and calculations C5, C6). Management's own measure is lower, with net debt to Adjusted EBITDA at 4.08x on USD 1,129.1 million of Adjusted EBITDA, because add-backs of USD 224.7 million, mostly technology implementation expense, separate it from the reported basis (Management Language, qualified; CP-1 financial table and calculation C9). A committee should anchor on the reported basis until the add-back bridge is tested.

Coverage has narrowed but is not yet strained. EBITDA to cash interest is 3.18x on USD 284.752 million of twelve-month cash interest, down from 5.29x in FY2025, because earnings fell while the 2035 notes and the revolver draw raised interest cost (Documentary Fact, CP-1 interest cover chart). Operating income to net interest expense is 1.05x, which shows how little earnings remain after depreciation and amortization once interest is paid, so a further margin decline would move coverage on that basis below parity (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 calculation C14).

Cash generation weakened as working capital absorbed cash. Operating cash flow for the nine months to September 30, 2026 was USD 302.031 million against USD 1,021.092 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 150.875 million; nine-month repurchases of USD 303.519 million exceeded that free cash flow by USD 152.644 million (Documentary Fact; calculation C3 below). The filing lists the share repurchases and the USD 197.0 million of net revolver borrowing together and does not say one funded the other, so that link is an inference, not a finding (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 cash uses). The mechanism for creditors is that cash that could reduce debt went to shareholders while leverage rose.

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main protections. Liquidity of USD 1,514.1 million is USD 55.012 million of cash plus USD 1,459.1 million of net revolver availability, far above the USD 173.2 million minimum at which the fixed charge test would apply, leaving USD 1,285.9 million of headroom to the trigger. No note or revolver matures before 2030, when USD 747.0 million falls due (the 5.00% notes and the drawn revolver), followed by USD 2,000.0 million in 2032, USD 1,000.0 million in 2034 and USD 750.0 million in 2035 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity, covenant and maturity sections). Two cautions apply: availability follows the borrowing base, so it can contract if receivables and inventory fall with sales, and qualified cash is counted in both cash and the borrowing base, so adding them may overstate liquidity by up to USD 21.3 million (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 liquidity basis).

The business is diversified but cyclical. The ten largest customers took 14% of FY2025 net sales and the largest 4%, and the largest supplier was 8% of purchases, so concentration is not the main risk (Documentary Fact; CP-1A customer and supplier rows). Net sales fell 2.2% in Q3 2026 on a lower housing starts environment and gross margin fell to 27.8% from 30.4%, and the company states significant fixed costs, so volume and price pressure flow through to cash flow quickly (Documentary Fact; CP-1A volume driver, margin and cost structure rows). Management cites USD 60 million to USD 70 million of expected 2026 productivity savings, which is a management claim not tested here (Management Language).

Capital allocation and governance are shareholder oriented but not documented as creditor adverse. The company has no sponsor or controlling holder documented, pays no dividend, has repurchased shares under successive programmes since August 2021 and completed acquisitions of USD 1.1 billion in 2025 and about USD 129.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A governance table). No priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release is documented, but the sources contain no indentures or current reports, so absence is not confirmed (Insufficient Information; CP-1A governance and gaps).

runs.text: Strengths. First, Builders FirstSource has a diversified customer and supplier base, with low single-name concentration that limits abrupt revenue or supply loss (Documentary Fact; CP-1A customers and suppliers rows). Second, it has ample liquidity relative to its covenant trigger: USD 1,514.1 million against USD 173.2 million, with a revolver of USD 2,200.0 million commitments maturing May 20, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and covenant sections). Third, its capital structure has no near-term maturity: fixed-rate senior unsecured notes mature from 2030 to 2035 and carry no scheduled amortization, which removes refinancing pressure until 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 maturity chart). Fourth, management describes a leading position with competitive advantages from scale, service and a broad product offering; this is management's characterisation and is not verified (Management Language; CP-1A positioning and products rows). Fifth, reporting is regular and includes reconciliations, which helps monitoring, though the add-backs are management defined (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance table).

Weaknesses. First, reported leverage is 5.15x total debt to EBITDA and 5.09x net, up from 3.26x and 3.12x in FY2025, and cover is 3.18x, so there is less room for earnings declines (Documentary Fact; CP-1 leverage and cover charts). Second, earnings are cyclical with significant fixed costs, and the latest quarter shows volume and margin declines tied to housing starts (Documentary Fact; CP-1A volume, margin and cost structure rows). Third, shareholder returns and acquisitions continued while earnings fell, with nine-month repurchases exceeding free cash flow, which slows deleveraging (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 cash uses, CP-1A governance table). Fourth, earnings quality depends on add-backs: Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 224.7 million, and the technology implementation line is large and not itemised (Documentary Fact for the difference; Analyst Interpretation for its quality; CP-1 reconciliation, CP-1A gaps). Fifth, structural and covenant protections cannot be verified because the credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list and beneficial ownership are not supplied, and unquantified construction defect claims exist (Insufficient Information; CP-0 and CP-1A gaps).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No transaction is pending, and no sponsor transaction, merger or refinancing was announced in the pinned sources between the end of the third quarter and the cutoff. The recent transaction history is in four parts. First, debt issuance: on February 29, 2024 the company issued 1.0 billion dollars of 6.375% senior unsecured notes due 2034, and on May 8, 2025 it issued 750.0 million dollars of 6.75% senior unsecured notes due 2035 at par, with the 2025 proceeds used to repay revolver borrowings [K10 page:92] "The net proceeds from the offering were used to repay indebtedness outstanding under the Revolving Facility." Second, the revolver was amended on May 20, 2025 to raise commitments from 1.8 billion to 2.2 billion dollars and extend maturity to May 20, 2030 [K10 page:92] "replace the existing revolving commitments of $1.8 billion with new revolving commitments of $2.2 billion, and to extend the maturity date to May 20, 2030". No new notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026; the revolver was drawn instead, with 197.0 million dollars outstanding at September 30, 2026 as set out in the financial handoff. Third, acquisitions: [K10 page:60] "During 2025, we completed a number of acquisitions for a combined $1.1 billion purchase price, net of cash acquired" across eight named businesses, then four more in the first nine months of 2026 for about 129.3 million dollars of consideration [Q3 page:9] "for a combined total purchase consideration of approximately $129.3 million", funded from cash and the revolver, with no pro forma information presented. Fourth, equity and strategic items: repurchases under authorizations renewed on April 30, 2025 and April 29, 2026, with 3.3 million shares bought for $302.9 million in the first nine months of 2026 and, per management, [R3 page:3] "The Company has $500 million remaining under its share repurchase authorization.", and a strategic investment in Digs, an AI platform, announced August 25, 2026 [Q3 page:22] "Under the partnership, the Company was the solo lead investor on Digs’ $25.3 million Series A financing". For each, the mechanics matter to a creditor: the note issues fixed the cost and pushed maturities to 2034 and 2035; the revolver amendment lengthened committed liquidity to 2030; acquisitions used cash and revolver capacity and added fixed cost and goodwill; repurchases reduce equity and cash; none changed the senior unsecured ranking. Key uncertainties are the covenant terms and guarantor perimeter, which the sources do not provide, and whether acquisition spending resumes at the 2025 pace.

fields.value: The financial base is sufficient to state the debt, earnings, cash flow and liquidity position of Builders FirstSource, Inc. at September 30, 2026, with the limitations listed under Gaps. Over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, reported earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization were well below FY2025 because gross margin fell and selling, general and administrative expense was broadly flat, while debt principal rose by 173.9 million, driven by 197.0 million of revolver borrowing. Total debt to EBITDA therefore moved from 3.26x to 5.15x and EBITDA to cash interest from 5.29x to 3.18x on the reported basis. Operating cash flow for the nine months to September 30, 2026 was 302.0 million against 1,021.1 million a year earlier, and the company repurchased 303.5 million of stock in the same nine months, almost all of it in the first quarter. Liquidity was 1,514.1 million at September 30, 2026 and stayed in a range of about 1.5 billion to 1.7 billion at the four balance dates read. The only financial covenant is a fixed charge coverage test of 1.00 to 1.00 that applies only if excess availability falls below a minimum; availability was far above it, and the ratio itself is not reported. The senior unsecured notes and the revolver are fixed in tenor, with the first maturity in 2030. The figures that most need a second look before use are the EBITDA definition (built here, not printed), the management Adjusted EBITDA that carries a large technology implementation add-back, and the guarantor perimeter, which no pinned source names.

Fair values at September 30, 2026 are printed per series (Q3 page:13). Notes are redeemable on terms in the indentures and carry a 101 percent change of control put; the indentures are not supplied.

fields.value: - Maintenance test: the revolver has one financial covenant, a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.00 to 1.00 that applies only when excess availability falls below the specified minimum. [K10 page:93] "of 1.00 to 1.00 if our excess availability falls below the greater of $165.0 million or 10% of the maximum borrowing amount, which was $160.7 million as of December 31, 2025."

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Level at September 30, 2026: [Q3 page:27] "Excess availability must equal or exceed a minimum specified amount, currently $173.2 million, or we are required to meet a fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.00 to 1.00." Reported availability is 1,459.1 million, so headroom to the trigger is 1,285.9 million (C15). The same calculation gives 1,257.9 million at March 31, 2026, 1,379.7 million at June 30, 2026 and 1,362.3 million at December 31, 2025 against the 165.0 million then in force. The threshold moves with the borrowing base (10 percent of 1,731.7 million is 173.17 million).

fields.value: - Leverage. Evidence: the debt table shows principal of 4,485,046 thousand at December 31, 2025 and 4,658,904 thousand at September 30, 2026, with the revolver drawn 197,000 thousand (Q3 page:13), while nine-month income from operations fell from 724,496 thousand to 244,113 thousand (Q3 page:2). Mechanism: the debt is largely fixed-rate notes with no scheduled principal payment before 2030, so leverage moves with earnings, and management attributes the gross profit decline mainly to a lower housing starts environment (R3 page:1). Implication: total debt to EBITDA is above the FY2025 level by about 1.9 turns on the reported basis, and further EBITDA decline raises it without any change in debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage. Evidence: net interest expense for nine months rose from 206,139 thousand to 222,740 thousand (Q3 page:2), and cash interest for the twelve months is 284,752 thousand (C2). Mechanism: the 6.75% 2035 notes were issued on May 8, 2025 and so were outstanding for only part of the nine-month 2025 comparator, and the revolver was drawn in 2026 (K10 page:92, Q3 page:13). Implication: fixed charges are stable to rising while EBITDA is falling, which is why cover moved from 5.29x to 3.18x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow. Evidence: nine-month operating cash flow of 302,031 thousand against 1,021,092 thousand (Q3 page:3), with working capital absorbing cash (Q3 page:28). Mechanism: receivables and inventories absorbed cash of 229,466 thousand and 122,131 thousand, partly offset by payables of 178,060 thousand (Q3 page:3). Implication: operating cash flow is already after cash interest, and free cash flow after capex of 150,875 thousand (C11) was positive but smaller than the repurchase of 303,519 thousand in the same period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity. Evidence: availability of 1,459.1 million against a trigger of 173.2 million (Q3 page:27). Mechanism: availability is borrowing-base driven, so it follows receivables and inventory and can contract as sales fall; the borrowing base grew from 1,606.9 million to 1,731.7 million as receivables and inventory rose, which offset part of the 197.0 million draw, so availability fell only from 1,527.3 million to 1,459.1 million. Implication: liquidity is currently ample, but part of it rests on the same working capital build that reduced operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maturities. Evidence: the maturity table above. Mechanism: no note or revolver is due before 2030 and the revolver and the 5.00% notes are both due in 2030, so refinancing risk concentrates in that year. Implication: no near-term refinancing pressure, with the 2030 date as the first test of market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Builders FirstSource, Inc. is a listed Delaware corporation that manufactures, supplies and installs structural building products for professional homebuilders and repair and remodel contractors, through roughly 575 locations in 43 states, organized into two geographic divisions reported as one segment. The business is cyclical and local: sales follow housing starts (net sales fell 2.2% in Q3 2026 on a lower housing starts environment), pricing is tied to service level and volume, and lumber is a commodity input and a sizeable sales category. The customer base is spread across large national production builders, regional and custom builders and contractors, so no single customer dominates, which supports revenue durability against single-name loss but not against a broad housing downturn, which is where 2026 stands. No sponsor, controlling shareholder, dividend recapitalisation or related-party leakage is documented in the sources. The transactions that matter to a creditor are the acquisition programme, the repurchase programme, the 2024 and 2025 senior unsecured note issues and the 2025 revolver amendment: together they explain why debt principal is higher while earnings are lower, as quantified in the financial handoff. Conduct is documented as shareholder-friendly through repurchases, and no creditor-adverse action is documented in the sources; legal capacity to distribute is limited by covenants whose terms are not supplied. The committee should treat what is missing as significant: the guarantor perimeter, the indentures and credit agreement, beneficial ownership and the end-market mix of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No transaction is pending, and no sponsor transaction, merger or refinancing was announced in the pinned sources between the end of the third quarter and the cutoff. The recent transaction history is in four parts. First, debt issuance: on February 29, 2024 the company issued 1.0 billion dollars of 6.375% senior unsecured notes due 2034, and on May 8, 2025 it issued 750.0 million dollars of 6.75% senior unsecured notes due 2035 at par, with the 2025 proceeds used to repay revolver borrowings [K10 page:92] "The net proceeds from the offering were used to repay indebtedness outstanding under the Revolving Facility." Second, the revolver was amended on May 20, 2025 to raise commitments from 1.8 billion to 2.2 billion dollars and extend maturity to May 20, 2030 [K10 page:92] "replace the existing revolving commitments of $1.8 billion with new revolving commitments of $2.2 billion, and to extend the maturity date to May 20, 2030". No new notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026; the revolver was drawn instead, with 197.0 million dollars outstanding at September 30, 2026 as set out in the financial handoff. Third, acquisitions: [K10 page:60] "During 2025, we completed a number of acquisitions for a combined $1.1 billion purchase price, net of cash acquired" across eight named businesses, then four more in the first nine months of 2026 for about 129.3 million dollars of consideration [Q3 page:9] "for a combined total purchase consideration of approximately $129.3 million", funded from cash and the revolver, with no pro forma information presented. Fourth, equity and strategic items: repurchases under authorizations renewed on April 30, 2025 and April 29, 2026, with 3.3 million shares bought for $302.9 million in the first nine months of 2026 and, per management, [R3 page:3] "The Company has $500 million remaining under its share repurchase authorization.", and a strategic investment in Digs, an AI platform, announced August 25, 2026 [Q3 page:22] "Under the partnership, the Company was the solo lead investor on Digs’ $25.3 million Series A financing". For each, the mechanics matter to a creditor: the note issues fixed the cost and pushed maturities to 2034 and 2035; the revolver amendment lengthened committed liquidity to 2030; acquisitions used cash and revolver capacity and added fixed cost and goodwill; repurchases reduce equity and cash; none changed the senior unsecured ranking. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Builders FirstSource's fundamental credit position is weakening, with liquidity still ample. The strongest support is USD 1,514.1 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026 against a revolver covenant trigger of USD 173.2 million, no note or revolver maturity before 2030, and a diversified customer and supplier base. The weakest point is reported EBITDA of USD 904.402 million over the last twelve months, which lifts total debt to EBITDA to 5.15x from 3.26x and lowers EBITDA to cash interest to 3.18x from 5.29x. The outcome depends on the housing cycle and on capital allocation: further gross margin erosion, or repurchases and acquisitions funded while earnings are low, would use up the cushion that liquidity and the maturity profile provide. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis: Builders FirstSource is a scaled, diversified building products supplier whose reported leverage has risen to 5.15x as housing weakness reduced earnings, but ample liquidity and a first maturity in 2030 give it time, so the credit turns on whether margins stabilise (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 leverage and liquidity figures, CP-1A credit translations on margin and cash-flow risk).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage has risen sharply. Debt principal at September 30, 2026 was USD 4,658.904 million against USD 4,485.046 million at December 31, 2025, an increase of USD 173.858 million driven by USD 197.0 million of revolver borrowing, while twelve-month reported EBITDA was USD 904.402 million against USD 1,377.708 million in FY2025. The debt is mostly fixed-rate senior unsecured notes with no scheduled principal payment before 2030, so leverage moves with earnings: total debt to EBITDA is 5.15x versus 3.26x and net debt to EBITDA 5.09x versus 3.12x (Documentary Fact, CP-1 leverage chart and calculations C5, C6). Management's own measure is lower, with net debt to Adjusted EBITDA at 4.08x on USD 1,129.1 million of Adjusted EBITDA, because add-backs of USD 224.7 million, mostly technology implementation expense, separate it from the reported basis (Management Language, qualified; CP-1 financial table and calculation C9). A committee should anchor on the reported basis until the add-back bridge is tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage has narrowed but is not yet strained. EBITDA to cash interest is 3.18x on USD 284.752 million of twelve-month cash interest, down from 5.29x in FY2025, because earnings fell while the 2035 notes and the revolver draw raised interest cost (Documentary Fact, CP-1 interest cover chart). Operating income to net interest expense is 1.05x, which shows how little earnings remain after depreciation and amortization once interest is paid, so a further margin decline would move coverage on that basis below parity (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 calculation C14).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation weakened as working capital absorbed cash. Operating cash flow for the nine months to September 30, 2026 was USD 302.031 million against USD 1,021.092 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 150.875 million; nine-month repurchases of USD 303.519 million exceeded that free cash flow by USD 152.644 million (Documentary Fact; calculation C3 below). The filing lists the share repurchases and the USD 197.0 million of net revolver borrowing together and does not say one funded the other, so that link is an inference, not a finding (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 cash uses). The mechanism for creditors is that cash that could reduce debt went to shareholders while leverage rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main protections. Liquidity of USD 1,514.1 million is USD 55.012 million of cash plus USD 1,459.1 million of net revolver availability, far above the USD 173.2 million minimum at which the fixed charge test would apply, leaving USD 1,285.9 million of headroom to the trigger. No note or revolver matures before 2030, when USD 747.0 million falls due (the 5.00% notes and the drawn revolver), followed by USD 2,000.0 million in 2032, USD 1,000.0 million in 2034 and USD 750.0 million in 2035 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity, covenant and maturity sections). Two cautions apply: availability follows the borrowing base, so it can contract if receivables and inventory fall with sales, and qualified cash is counted in both cash and the borrowing base, so adding them may overstate liquidity by up to USD 21.3 million (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 liquidity basis).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified but cyclical. The ten largest customers took 14% of FY2025 net sales and the largest 4%, and the largest supplier was 8% of purchases, so concentration is not the main risk (Documentary Fact; CP-1A customer and supplier rows). Net sales fell 2.2% in Q3 2026 on a lower housing starts environment and gross margin fell to 27.8% from 30.4%, and the company states significant fixed costs, so volume and price pressure flow through to cash flow quickly (Documentary Fact; CP-1A volume driver, margin and cost structure rows). Management cites USD 60 million to USD 70 million of expected 2026 productivity savings, which is a management claim not tested here (Management Language).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation and governance are shareholder oriented but not documented as creditor adverse. The company has no sponsor or controlling holder documented, pays no dividend, has repurchased shares under successive programmes since August 2021 and completed acquisitions of USD 1.1 billion in 2025 and about USD 129.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A governance table). No priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release is documented, but the sources contain no indentures or current reports, so absence is not confirmed (Insufficient Information; CP-1A governance and gaps).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, Builders FirstSource has a diversified customer and supplier base, with low single-name concentration that limits abrupt revenue or supply loss (Documentary Fact; CP-1A customers and suppliers rows). Second, it has ample liquidity relative to its covenant trigger: USD 1,514.1 million against USD 173.2 million, with a revolver of USD 2,200.0 million commitments maturing May 20, 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and covenant sections). Third, its capital structure has no near-term maturity: fixed-rate senior unsecured notes mature from 2030 to 2035 and carry no scheduled amortization, which removes refinancing pressure until 2030 (Documentary Fact; CP-1 maturity chart). Fourth, management describes a leading position with competitive advantages from scale, service and a broad product offering; this is management's characterisation and is not verified (Management Language; CP-1A positioning and products rows). Fifth, reporting is regular and includes reconciliations, which helps monitoring, though the add-backs are management defined (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance table).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, reported leverage is 5.15x total debt to EBITDA and 5.09x net, up from 3.26x and 3.12x in FY2025, and cover is 3.18x, so there is less room for earnings declines (Documentary Fact; CP-1 leverage and cover charts). Second, earnings are cyclical with significant fixed costs, and the latest quarter shows volume and margin declines tied to housing starts (Documentary Fact; CP-1A volume, margin and cost structure rows). Third, shareholder returns and acquisitions continued while earnings fell, with nine-month repurchases exceeding free cash flow, which slows deleveraging (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 cash uses, CP-1A governance table). Fourth, earnings quality depends on add-backs: Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 224.7 million, and the technology implementation line is large and not itemised (Documentary Fact for the difference; Analyst Interpretation for its quality; CP-1 reconciliation, CP-1A gaps). Fifth, structural and covenant protections cannot be verified because the credit agreement, indentures, guarantor list and beneficial ownership are not supplied, and unquantified construction defect claims exist (Insufficient Information; CP-0 and CP-1A gaps).
